Subject: Renewal proposal: term extension + HW swap (A100 → H100)

Hi Claire / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the conversation today. As discussed, below is a concise proposal to align the upcoming renewal with Zephyr's performance and cost objectives. High level: move the committed pool from A100→H100, add 8 additional GPUs (reserved pool), and extend the term to 12 months to enable the HW transition at a discounted unit rate.

Why H100 for this workload
- Throughput: our internal tests on Zephyr-like LLMs show H100 yields ~1.7–1.9x sustained token throughput vs A100 at typical 2k seq lengths.
- Cost: list price per-hour is higher, but combined with improved batching and fewer instances needed, the net cost-per-token improves by ~25–35% depending on utilization.
- Latency SLOs: H100 reduces tail latency for concurrent small requests (important for your interactive use case).

Proposal (summary)
- Term: 12 months (start on renewal date)
- Reserved capacity: +8 H100 GPUs (in addition to existing committed 24 A100-equivalent units)
- Migration: Redwood will perform the switchover with a canary pool and KV-cache migration window to minimize customer impact
- Throughput guarantee: 99th percentile per-request token latency target and a baseline throughput floor (details in attached pricing annex)
- Commercial: blended committed rate that reflects the term extension and reserved add-on (pricing PDF attached)

Attached: H100_benchmark_summary.csv, Zephyr_Renewal_Prices_Q3_2026.pdf

Next steps
1) I can send a draft SOW and pricing annex for procurement review (SOW + DocuSign)
2) Neha can run an on-demand benchmark on Zephyr's prod-ish workload next week (need safe sample prompts)
3) If you confirm we’ll hold the quoted capacity for 7 days while procurement reviews

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the economics.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin

- Monica: prepare a concise commercial annex — line-item rates, term-level discounts, and the recommended guardrail (we hold quoted capacity for 7 days). Also include the canary migration plan and fallback policy language for capacity constraints.

Initial performance notes (rough numbers, do not share externally yet):
- A100 baseline: 1.0x throughput, $0.75 effective unit cost per 1M tokens
- H100 swap: ~1.8x throughput, $1.02 effective unit cost per-hour → net $0.52 per 1M tokens (approx 30% lower cost-per-token at 70% utilization)
- L40S burst: 1.5x throughput vs A100 for large batches, ~0.9x relative to H100 for small-concurrency interactive; attractive for batch-only workloads but weaker on tail latency

Can you assemble the CSV/figures and a one-page slide for Claire? If you need test prompts from Zephyr, Marcus — please request their safe sample set.

Marcus
